patient.name: Maya Okafor
patient.background: First-year university student, rugby player, no medical history, new boyfriend

initial_symptoms.text: Very sore throat, white patches on tonsils

findings.result: Many large odd white cells: atypical lymphocytes
Marrow active but normal, no leukemia cells: reactive hyperplasia
Swollen tonsils, white exudate, airway open: tonsillitis
Rapid strep test negative: no Streptococcus
Fast but normal rhythm: sinus tachycardia
No neck stiffness, no swelling: meningitis ruled out
Tiny red dots on palate: petechiae

treatments.name: Rest, fluids, no contact sports
treatments.why: EBV is viral and clears on its own; avoiding sport protects the swollen spleen from rupturing.
treatments.attending_line: Doing nothing, correctly. Rarest skill in medicine. Don't let it go to your head.

treatments.name: Amoxicillin (antibiotic)
treatments.why: Antibiotics don't kill viruses, and amoxicillin with EBV triggers a widespread itchy rash in most patients.

if_wrong_cascade.text: Itchy red rash over whole body
Diarrhea from gut bacteria wiped out

treatments.attending_line: Congratulations, you've painted her pink. The virus is unimpressed.

treatments.name: Clear her for rugby
treatments.why: Mono enlarges the spleen, and a tackle can rupture it, causing major internal bleeding.

if_wrong_cascade.text: Sudden blood loss, pale and faint
Sharp left belly and shoulder pain

treatments.attending_line: Great plan. Let's also juggle knives. The spleen thanks you, briefly.

treatments.name: High-dose acetaminophen around the clock
treatments.why: Her liver is already inflamed by EBV; heavy acetaminophen adds toxic strain on it.
treatments.attending_line: Her liver was already sick. You decided it needed homework.

post_mortem: Maya picked up Epstein-Barr virus through saliva and got mononucleosis, which looks a lot like strep throat. The negative strep test, atypical lymphocytes, extreme tiredness and shared water bottle all pointed to the 'kissing disease', not bacteria.
